assumptions: Task ends when the verification result (with human understanding UNKNOWN) is visible: TTFV-2 in docs/hci/design/content-and-onboarding.md section 7.
KLM is invalid for first-time users (LAW section 2.4): the flow is an expert, error-free FLOOR, not an estimate of novice time. A novice takes longer; the study measures the real value.

Reading is modelled outside KLM as R operations at 250 wpm (NN/g assumed rate; band 180 to 250 wpm gives the low-to-high range) over NOVEL words only (words not on the previous screen); it assumes every word is read, which is an upper bound (NN/g 2008: users read at most about 28% of words on average pages).

Word counts: current = MEASURED from index.html (alphanumeric tokens) plus hand-counted dynamic strings from app.js, policy.py and providers.py; proposed = the drafts in the doc section 8, a design cap not a measurement.

Current flow uses the default offline provider and the prefilled request; ids follow the current-* layout files (button is the supported card's Select meaning button, case-item is the case list entry, tab-evidence, q-*, acknowledge).
Proposed flow assumes the layout lane keeps HOME open-sample as a single primary action and a Next slot on REVIEW; element ids are proposed interface names to be mapped by the layout lane.
Local API calls assumed 100 ms each (unmeasured); the verification time is MEASURED and equal in both flows.
Proposed sample creation needs create plus propose with the offline provider, which the current API allows without consent; with a networked provider the sample opens the case only (doc section 7).

P operations name a layout stem where both element ids exist in one current-* layout (request to create; propose to button to tab-evidence; tab-evidence to verify). The create to propose step crosses screens and the proposed ids are not in a layout, so those use the default P of 1.1 s. Geometry is in page coordinates and scrolling between elements is not modelled.

T10's proposed flow has 3 required clicks; the current flow has 5. Reading time is an upper bound (every novel word read); NN/g reports that readers read about 20 to 28 percent of words on typical web pages, so the reading totals are a sensitivity range in HCI-ADR-0065, not an estimate.

assumptions: Variant of brief task T08 (approve and apply the exact revision, P1, daily). Frequency is set to weekly because recovery happens on a fraction of approvals; that fraction is unknown (deviation from the parent's daily, a hypothesis).

Trigger is STALE_VERSION (case changed elsewhere, for example by the CLI or another tab). The baseline clears the approval form on reload (page reload). The proposal keeps the typed answers in place but CLEARS the acknowledgement of UNKNOWNs whenever the case version changed, so the owner re-acknowledges on the changed case (I4, P2). This costs one M, one P and one B and 6 more words to read compared with the first draft.

This is the MOUSE-ONLY baseline (pointer between every answer field, H around each typed answer). It is a novice-like or strawman path and is reported for completeness. The expert baseline is T08-recover-stale-kbd, which types and Tabs through the fields; that is the comparison the ADR treats as primary.
The re-review time (10 s) is an assumption and is identical in all flows so that the design cannot appear faster by skipping review; the decision surface must still re-show the changed items.

Preserving typed answers is a client behaviour, not a kernel change; approval still needs the exact subject hash, so a changed subject blocks approval regardless (SUBJECT_CHANGED). Answers are kept only for questions whose id and text are unchanged.
Current answers are 9, 2 and 11 characters (Registrar, No, Recommended): the expected answers from meaning_questions in policy.py.

H operators: 8 in this baseline (hand to keyboard and back around F5, and around each of the three typed answers), 0 in the proposed flow, which has no typing. The current P operators use geometry from current-evidence (page coordinates; scrolling between elements is not modelled).

assumptions: Variant of brief task T06 (run and read verification evidence, P4, daily); persona and frequency match the parent.

Trigger is one blocker: RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_UNKNOWN with the meaning already selected. The current line reads 3 words; the proposed header and row read 8 words (BLOCKED, 1, reason, Runtime evidence UNKNOWN, Run verification).

The proposed saving is one M operator (1.35 s) for decoding the raw code, against 1.2 s of extra reading; the net difference is inside the KLM band of plus or minus 21%, so this task is a consistency check, not evidence.
Verification time is MEASURED and identical in both flows.
